why: One 30-minute slot holds several shorter cartoons, and the two sides punctuate the combination differently: the submitter writes 'Colossal Squid / Jawfish', the registry stores 'Colossal Squid; Jawfish'. Until eidr-core 0.26.0 segments() split only on '/', so one side was two segments and the other was one, and the pair scored EXACTLY 0.500 on the field this engine weights most heavily. Two confirmed matches were closed as terminal no-match on that alone (BMR-Review scoring review, 2026-09-01). The lesson is version-independent and belongs in an invariant rather than a value: a delimiter list must never decide identity. Same set, either punctuation, any order -- one program. MUTATION-TESTED, with a limitation worth stating: this pair fails against the FULL pre-0.26.0 comparator (both the invariant and the snapshot), but it does NOT isolate the ';' delimiter on its own. norm_title already strips ';', so with ';' removed from segments() the one-side-delimited token_sort_ratio fallback still returns 1.0 and the pair passes. It is an end-to-end regression pair for the reported defect, not a unit probe for the delimiter list; a pair that isolates the delimiter would need segment sets that differ after normalisation.
